$comment: SeaBus operating assumptions. Geometry (berths, lanes) is in data/infrastructure/seabus.json. OPEN-QUESTIONS #24.
$pair: The berth every vessel uses at each terminal. On a given day all vessels use west–west or east–east, with rare exceptions: the wheelhouse sees the passenger ramps better from one side, so a vessel always loads facing the same way (Braden, 2026-09-28). The timetable allows it: one vessel leaves at least 7 min before the next arrives, even at the weekday peak. Which pair is used varies by day and isn't known in advance; west is from the one sighting (Burrard Pacific Breeze at the West berths, 2026-09-26 14:15/14:29, Braden). guess
$ais: Live vessel positions from aisstream.io (PLAN.md §4.12; key AISSTREAM_API_KEY in .secrets). The RT service's leader keeps one WebSocket open, records fixes to data/ais-history/ and serves them at /rt/ais/fixes; the browser turns them into timetable anchors (src/core/ais/match.ts).

ais.$vessels: MMSIs from MarineTraffic / VesselFinder / MyShipTracking, cross-checked (2026-09-28). Burrard Beaver is the spare.
ais.$boundingBox: Burrard Inlet around the crossing and the layup berth, [[lat, lon], [lat, lon]] (aisstream order).
ais.$batchS: Fixes are recorded in batches this often (an empty batch while connected keeps recorder coverage going).
ais.$maxBackoffS: Reconnect backoff doubles from 5 s up to this.
ais.$match: Matching fixes to trips. Probe 2026-09-29: fixes arrive in bursts (receivers upload intermittently), minutes apart; docked positions agree with the berth dock points to ~5 m. Guesses unless noted; OPEN-QUESTIONS #27.

match.$maxOffsetM: Lanes are traced to ±30 m and vessels wander ~100 m around them (AIS tracks).
match.$minTurnaroundS: Timetabled layovers are 2–4 min; a late vessel catches up by shortening them to this.
